# P1-19 — Task traceability

**Generated by `scripts/p1-19-endpoint-inventory.mjs`. Do not hand-edit.**

Each row joins one operation to the route that exposes it, the permission that
guards it, the audit action it writes, the module code that performs it, and the
test file the coverage gate credits it to — with that gate’s own evidence flags,
not this script’s opinion of them.

## The annotation collision is real, and is not tidied away

**7** of the 18 annotated identifiers reach operations in **two
different schemas**: P1-19-BE-009, P1-19-BE-010, P1-19-BE-011, P1-19-BE-012, P1-19-BE-017, P1-19-BE-018, P1-19-BE-019. `BE-009`, for instance, reaches
both `wo.job-create` and the four diagnostic-report operations; `BE-017` reaches
both the quality-control record surface and two labour-session operations. The
cause is mundane: the work-order and technician waves annotated their files
before the additional-work, diagnostics and QMS waves did, and the two
numberings were assigned independently.

Same-schema breadth is a separate matter and is not called a collision here.
`BE-006` reaches six `wo` operations spanning the work-order list and the
additional-work request surface, which may be one task or two — without the
canonical titles there is no way to tell, so no claim is made either way.

The canonical Phase 1 Development Plan, which is the only authority on what each
identifier means, lives outside this repository by owner decision. So the
collision **cannot be resolved here**, and renumbering the annotations to make
this table look tidy would replace a visible inconsistency with an invisible
invention. The annotations are left exactly as the implementing commits made
them and the ambiguity is recorded as an open finding (`P1-19-A-03`).

What this table can and does establish, independently of the identifiers, is
that **every operation P1-19 exposes is guarded, audited where it changes state,
implemented in a module, and covered by an assertion-backed test at operation
depth**. That is the claim a reviewer needs; the identifier is a label on it.
